items.t: "add to the… zero to hero income BOLO… I can actually create voices in ElevenLabs. That could be something I can definitely do."

The asset Chief named is the skill, not the tool: building voices in ElevenLabs is something he can already do today, with no ramp — the same standing order as BOLO 24 (start now with what is in hand).

BOLO 56 already ruled ElevenLabs as JUDY's eventual voice and wired it the same session — `speak.py` fronts sapi · piper · elevenlabs behind one `say()`, the official SDK (2.68.0) integrated. One subscription would serve the venture and the crew at once.

Four candidate paths, unranked and unverified: the ElevenLabs Voice Library payout program (share a voice, earn on usage) · built-to-order voices for creators, studios, game devs and audiobook work · a voice for BOLO 24's disclosed 3D persona · narration/VO delivered as a service on Chief's own editing strength.
Not costed. The payout terms, the rates, the exclusivity and the licensing on any voice he builds are all unverified — nothing here should be ranked until a boresight prices it.

The real question is the one BOLO 29 already asks: which venture starts first. This makes that a four-way, not a three-way — 24 · 27 · 29 · 57 — and per STATE's Blocked #11 it can't be ruled until 57 gets a boresight.

**DOPE SHEET 57 is live** and recorded in `BOLO.md` row 57, `_tools/pages/pages.json` and the `bolo57` glossary key (created 9/17 — it did not exist). The row was also placed on the board for the first time on 2026-09-16-6, **held on a ruling**; the WATCH specialist had dropped it and the assembler's checklist caught it.
**The tool is owned.** When this row was captured the ElevenLabs cost was a reason to rank it below the other three; it is now $0 marginal, because BOLO 56 pays for the account regardless.

**The skill is demonstrated, not claimed.** Chief's four-voice audition and the stability/style dial test are the first evidence he can actually shape a voice to a brief — which is the whole asset this row rests on.
Payout terms, per-character rates, exclusivity, and what rights he keeps on a voice he builds. **None of it verified.** The ranking on Blocked #11 cannot close until it is.

items.t: **Sell in the ElevenLabs Voice Library at studio grade** (Chief 9/24: "super high quality … emotional weight, speed, tempo"). Fiverr PARKED.
**The one rule:** the clone only does what it heard — emotion, tempo and range must be on the recording; it copies every flaw and every bit of processing.
**Size:** ~2:50 of finished audio across 8 packs (ElevenLabs: 30 min minimum, 2–3 h for pro); 4–5 h at the mic; all of it inside one 24–48 h window.
**RØDE NT1 Signature → XLR → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 (2nd/3rd gen) → Ableton Live.** Nothing in between.
**Stock pop filter is fine**; add a ~$15 metal mesh only if P/B still pop after angling the mic off-axis.
**Tube preamp: out** for the clone (color + hiss get cloned). Test it later for character demos: its output into the Scarlett's line input, phantom power in one place only.
**Scarlett:** 48V on · INST off · AIR off (3rd gen) · Direct Monitor on, Ableton monitor Off · halo green, amber only on the loudest lines, never red · Focusrite USB ASIO driver.
**Average (RMS) -23 to -18 dBFS, aim -20** · **true peak never above -3** · **room noise -60 or lower** (the first two are ElevenLabs'; the third is voice-over practice).
**Set the gain once:** loudest line (Pack 2, urgent) peaks near -6 · a calm read sits near -20 · 10 s of silence at -60 or lower · lock the gain for both days.
**Reading the meters:** the free Youlean Loudness Meter (short-term LUFS ≈ RMS for speech; true-peak readout) · Ableton's meter bounces -12 to -8 on normal talk.

**No compression, no EQ curves, no reverb, no heavy noise reduction on clone audio.** One allowed exception: a gentle low cut at 70–80 Hz (EQ Eight). After recording: normalize the peaks to -3 and nothing else.
**The polish chain is for demos and deliveries only:** low cut → gentle EQ → compressor → de-esser → limiter.
**Setup:** Focusrite ASIO, 48 kHz · WAV, 24-bit · Auto-Warp Long Samples OFF · one mono track, armed, monitor Off · Youlean on the track.

**Cut and export:** split Ctrl+E, delete flubs, fillers, loud breaths and every duplicate read · export WAV 48k/24, Normalize OFF · MP3 via `ffmpeg -i take.wav -codec:a libmp3lame -b:a 320k take.mp3`.
**Keep the recorder rolling:** one take = one script block (~2 min); 10–15 min sections; ~2 s of silence between takes.
**Flub:** 3 s of silence, reread from the start of the sentence. Wrong energy: reread the take and keep the better one. Read each take silently first.
**Read from a tablet at eye level beside the mic**, never paper; tap to advance (mouse wheels click). No filming. Sit or stand the same both days (rec: tall stool). Talk to one person.

**The $22 verdict (9/24):** month-one earnings probably won't cover Creator (the 9/23 boresight: library $10–50 over 90 days on target). Record now at $0, pay only on upload day, run 90 days, cut it if the voice hasn't earned back one month's $22 by day 90. First check the plan JUDY's account is on: if it's already Creator, the marginal cost is $0. Unverified: whether a shared clone survives a downgrade.

**Earnings tiers per voice per month:** bottom half $0–5 · median ~$10–30 · mean ~$175 (ElevenLabs: $11M in 6 months ÷ 10,400+ creators) · top 10% ~$300–1,000 · top 1% ~$3,000–10,000+ (anchored by a $4k/month top earner in 3/2024). Only the mean is computed from ElevenLabs' numbers; the other tiers are estimates.

**Several voices, one at a time:** narrator → gremlin → sidekick → mentor → villain. Each new voice must serve a different buyer; add #2 after 30–60 days of narrator data. Each voice is its own 2–3 h of recording; PVC slot counts per plan are unverified.
